program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is malformed and underspecified: it contains a dangling “visibly (...)” fragment, then a question, while the node’s actual criterion refers to a single flower although the source has one rose and the edit shows two flowers. Make the binding a clear, executable visual criterion tied to the requested book–flower depth relation, and ensure it distinguishes actual foreground occlusion/depth evidence from mere proximity or left/right placement. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress distinction: the edited image shows the book and flowers still separate, with no visible overlap, so unrelated changes (including the altered book and flowers) are not progress; do not infer absence from those changes alone. Keep unresolved evidence unknown. The repeated high-confidence failures support the no-progress assessment, but the final unknown is explicitly caused by transport/SSL failures, not contrary visual evidence; do not encode that as a visual fail or alter the criterion to force the reference label. Improve dependency handling/retry or preserve unknown when required checks cannot run.
s2: Repair the malformed, dangling binding so it is a single clear visual test of progress toward the requested depth relation, comparing the book with the flower(s) in the edited image. Require evidence consistent with the book moving behind a flower—such as overlap with the flower visibly in front of the book—and distinguish this from mere proximity, lateral repositioning, or unrelated object changes. Preserve the partial-progress rule: a changed position counts only when it evidences movement toward that relation; do not require full completion to pass. In these images the book and flowers remain separate, with no visible occlusion, so the repeated valid high-confidence failures support no progress; the altered book and flowers are not themselves progress. Keep genuinely indeterminate visual evidence unknown. The remaining unknown trace is explicitly an SSL/transport failure, not visual evidence: handle retries or retain unknown when execution fails rather than converting it into a visual judgment. Avoid changing the criterion merely to force the aggregate reference label.
s1: Repair the binding’s dangling, malformed wording into one executable test of the requested book–flower depth relation. Compare the book with the flower(s) actually visible in the edited image; assess foreground/occlusion evidence, not proximity or left/right placement. Preserve partial-progress semantics: count only visible change that moves the book toward being behind a flower, not unrelated edits or object changes. The traces consistently report the book and flowers remain separate with no occlusion, supporting no progress here; do not force that conclusion when visual evidence is genuinely indeterminate. Keep transport/schema failures distinct from visual judgments: the final unknown is an SSL transport failure, so retry or retain unknown rather than treating it as evidence for or against the edit. Repeated high-confidence results are useful evidence, but variation or low confidence alone does not establish whether the requested change is absent.
